subject: Mechanical Engineering
title: Hydraulic Filters: Keeping Oil Clean
description: A micro-lesson that makes Hydraulic Filters: Keeping Oil Clean usable.

hook.text: Particles smaller than a grain of sand can destroy a hydraulic pump. Filters keep the oil clean.

buildup.text: Metal shavings, rubber fragments, and dirt circulate in used oil. They wedge between precision surfaces and score them.

discovery.text: A 10-micron filter catches particles invisible to the naked eye. Most hydraulic failures trace back to contamination.

twist.text: New oil isn't clean enough. It must be filtered before entering the system. Even fresh oil carries contaminants.

climax.text: Changing filters on schedule costs a few dollars. Replacing a destroyed pump costs thousands. Prevention wins.

punchline.text: Clean oil runs forever. Dirty oil destroys everything.

quiz.question: Why must even new hydraulic oil be filtered before use?
options: New oil is too thick and must be filtered to reduce viscosity
Even fresh oil from the container carries invisible contaminants
Filtering adds necessary chemical additives to the oil
